lines.text: Many learners say: I made a claim to the store.
Better: I made a complaint to the store.
Use complaint when you say something is wrong.
Complaint! I made a complaint to the store.

data.wrong: I made a claim to the store.
data.right: I made a complaint to the store.
data.why: Use complaint when you say something is wrong.

native.hook: 「クレーム」は claim じゃない？
native.tip: カタカナの「クレーム」は complaint のこと。claim は「主張」や「請求」の意味です。
native.caption: “I made a claim to the store.”と言っていませんか？😅 「クレーム」をそのまま claim と言いがちです。“I made a complaint to the store.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“complaint”。同じ形で自分の文を1つ書いてみよう。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: The katakana word ``claim'' means complaint. Claim means "claim" or "request."
en.caption: Do you say this? “I made a claim to the store.” 😅 Claim is not the word for complaint. The natural way is “I made a complaint to the store.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
